claims.statement: For every fixed eligible tree instance, quotienting its deletion-plus-two-for-one weighted transport by a finite automorphism group that preserves the fixed original selector, weights, and legal moves preserves saturating-flow feasibility exactly.
claims.scope: Finite tree instance at its specified rank and selector; the general finite-group orbit-lifting proposition is proved in REPORT.md and EVIDENCE.json. This gives no uniform bound over all eligible trees.
claims.reason: Flows aggregate over vertex orbits. Every nonempty invariant relation between two transitive vertex orbits is biregular, so a quotient flow can be spread uniformly over literal edges while preserving per-vertex loads. The literal integral network then has an integral saturating flow whenever the quotient is feasible.

claims.statement: The weighted transport is feasible exactly when every upper-state set X satisfies u(X)<=c(N(X)); the cut deficit c(N(X))-u(X) is submodular and its minimizers are closed under union and intersection.
claims.scope: All finite bipartite weighted transport instances with the stated legal relation; this is a criterion and minimizer structure, not a proof that all tree-derived cuts pass.
claims.reason: This follows from the capacitated Hall/max-flow min-cut theorem and the submodularity of weighted neighborhood coverage minus a modular supply function. The universal tree cut inequalities remain unproved.

claims.statement: The Frankl-Füredi-Kalai colored one-step shadow theorem does not by itself imply the fixed-selector weighted deletion-plus-two-for-one cut inequalities.
claims.scope: Application check for the cited theorem against the present transport relation; it is not a refutation of any possible refinement or of the primary aggregate.
claims.reason: The cited theorem counts unweighted subset shadows, while legal switches insert an absent vertex and the present capacities are selector-dependent weights. A separate bridge accounting for switches and competing capacities is missing.

limitations: No universal cut classification, capacitated Hall proof, eligible full-sum counterexample, or resolution of the primary aggregate is obtained.
The automorphism quotient is exact but may be large; asymmetric trees can have little compression.
The colored-shadow literature result has no direct application to switch arcs or selector-weighted capacities without additional proved structure.
The source packet and handoff contain finite instrument results and a partial choked-broom export only; those scopes are not enlarged here.
